title: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness

draft.title: Prevention, mitigation and preparedness
card: Prevention
stops harm from happening at all. An example is not allowing houses to be built on land that floods often.
Mitigation
reduces the harm when a hazard still happens. Examples are levees, which are banks that hold back river water, and building rules for strong homes.
Preparedness
gets people ready before a hazard arrives. Examples are warning systems, emergency kits and evacuation plans.
These steps cannot stop a hazard such as a cyclone or a flood. They aim to lower the harm to people and property.
draft.remember: Prevention stops harm, mitigation lessens it, and preparedness readies people.

a.q: A council in Tasmania sets up a text message alert so residents hear when a river is rising. What is this?
opts: Preparedness, because it helps people get ready
Prevention, because it stops the river from rising
Mitigation, because it holds back the river water
A hazard, because it makes the river more dangerous
a.why: A warning gets people ready to act before the flood arrives, so it is preparedness. It does not stop the river rising, which would be prevention, or hold water back, which is what a levee does.
a.clue: The alert tells people something before the flood arrives.

b.q: A town in the Northern Territory requires new houses to be built with strong roofs that can resist cyclone winds. Which is the best description of this rule?
opts: Mitigation, because it reduces damage from cyclone winds
Prevention, because it stops cyclones from forming
Preparedness, because it warns people a cyclone is coming
A hazard, because cyclones damage roofs
b.why: Strong roofs do not stop a cyclone, but they reduce the damage it does, so the rule is mitigation. Prevention would stop the harm from happening at all, and a building rule does not warn anyone.
b.clue: Can a roof stop a cyclone, or only lessen the damage?

a.best: Preparedness, because it helps people get ready

b.best: Mitigation, because it reduces damage from cyclone winds

problems.detail: The last bullet says all these steps 'aim to lower the harm', but the first bullet says prevention 'stops harm from happening at all'. This could confuse students about how prevention differs from mitigation. Consider wording such as 'They aim to stop or lower the harm to people and property.'
